newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee at standstill, prices inch up.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee at standstill, prices inch up.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures trading was virtually at a standstill on Monday with a meagre 253 lots changing hands and prices stood a shade higher by midsession.
Traders said light trade selling was well taken out, and light buying then emerged.
"Apart from that, the market is dead," said one trader.
September was traded from $1,590 to $1,610 before finishing $3 up at $1,608 on a volume of 194.
Market participants were said to have turned to the more active cocoa futures which saw heavy spec long liquidation.

On the fundamental front, traders in London played down concerns voiced by some quarters in the U.S. trade over the weekend that a hurricane could potentially damange coffee stored in New Orleans warehouses or disrupt coffee shipments to New Orleans.
"There is a hurricane in New Orleans and some people were afraid it could hit warehouses," one U.S. trader said one Friday.
But traders in London said only heavy rains were forecast in that area.
Monday is the last day for trading of July contract on the New York futures.
The U.S. CFTC Commitment of Traders report on Friday showed the most balanced picture in a long while, broker GNI said.
The commercial side is only marginally net short and the funds only marginally long.
"This is a recipe for stability - a fund sell-off would probably be met with roaster buying, while a rally would see producer selling," it said.
